_comment: Routine names supported by evidence, applied by tools/disasm_all.py. Key 'BB:AAAA'. A name describes what the routine provably does (read from its instructions, or confirmed on the emulator) and never a guessed game purpose. 'note' gives inputs and outputs. The address name (Func_BBB_AAAA) is kept as an alias label. Evidence ids refer to docs/EVIDENCE_LOG.md; 'reading' means a complete static reading of the routine's instructions (E-0022).

00:1F89.name: LoadSRAMRecordWord

00:1FD1.name: SRAMRecordAddress
00:1FD1.note: A = record, C = offset; HL = sA000 + A * $A5 + C (records are $A5 bytes)

E0:7480.name: IncrementSpriteSlotCounters

E0:7492.name: StepSpriteSlotToward
E0:7492.note: A = slot number, D = target X, E = target Y: moves the slot's X and Y bytes one step toward the target and adds 1 to its byte 7; returns A = 1 (non-zero) if either moved

E0:74C5.name: SetSpriteSlotByte5
E0:74C5.note: A = slot number: byte 5 of the slot = C

E0:755E.name: StepWD0A2Mod30
E0:755E.note: wD0A2 += 1, reset to 0 when it reaches 30

E0:757C.note: wD0A2 += 1, reset to 0 when it reaches 60

00:0DF2.name: StartPaletteFade
00:0DF2.note: A = level (bit 7 set selects the second form); on CGB it hands over to Func_002_4001; on DMG it rebuilds the palette copy at wC4FF from wC4DF and sets wC56C, wC572-wC574, with $7FFF (white) or $0000 (black) fill chosen by bit 7 of wC56D; observed writes only, the purpose is a palette fade by inference

03:42DA.name: CopyTileBufferToBGMap
03:42DA.note: copies the 20 x 18 tiles at the start of wScreenTileBuffer to vBGMap0 (CopyRectToBGMap with BC = $1412)

03:42E3.name: CopyRectToBGMap
03:42E3.note: HL = BG map address, DE = source, B = width, C = rows: writes B bytes per row with WriteVRAMByte (HL wraps inside its 32-entry row, then the source and destination each move down 32 and HL is masked with $9B)

00:21A1.name: CopyGlyphTilesToVRAM
00:21A1.note: DE = VRAM destination: for each byte of the string at wC8CF (up to 11, stopping at $F0), copies the 16-byte tile at ROM bank $1F, $4010 + 16 * character to [DE]; the characters $8D and $8E also OR a 16-byte overlay from $48E0 or $48F0 into the previous tile

33:4001.name: CopyBlockToTileBuffer
33:4001.note: DE = block number: the table at $405F gives each block an offset into wScreenTileBuffer (word), a width B and a height C, followed by B * C tile bytes; they are copied into wScreenTileBuffer rows 32 bytes apart

5F:6BCD.name: AddStepDeltaToPointedByte
5F:6BCD.note: the byte at the address in wC928/wC929 += the byte at Func_05F_6BE8 + wC921 / 2

00:2123.name: WriteDecimalDigitTiles
00:2123.note: DE = destination: writes three tile ids for the digits in wC8C0-wC8C2 (see HLToDecimalDigits): $E0 + digit, with leading zeros as $C3; DE ends past the third

12:7DCE.name: FindHFFC6InWC61DList
12:7DCE.note: hFFC6 = the index of the first byte of the 24-entry list at wC61D equal to hFFC6; $FF when an entry is $00 or $FF first or no entry matches

00:173A.name: Number24ToPackedBCD
00:173A.note: the 24-bit value at wC8C0-wC8C2 (low byte first) becomes decimal digits: hFFC9 = millions, hFFC8 = hundred-thousands and ten-thousands, hFFC7 = thousands and hundreds, hFFC6 = tens and ones (two digits per byte, high digit in the upper nibble); wC8C0-wC8C2 are consumed

00:1FA4.name: CopyRecordNameToWC8CF
00:1FA4.note: A = record number, C = offset (see SRAMRecordAddress): copies 10 bytes from the SRAM record to wC8CF; when the first byte is $FF it writes $98,$98,$98,$90,$90 instead and sets carry; DE and HL are preserved

F1:5834.name: BeginString_Bank0E_Cat0
F1:5834.note: A = string index: wStringIndex = A, wStringCategory = 0, then BeginStringDisplay_Bank0E

1F:5040.name: SendSGBPacketSet
1F:5040.note: returns at once when wSGBActive is 0; otherwise sends the packet set chosen by wSGBPacketIndex ($FF = the buffer at wSGBPacketBuffer, else the pointer in the table at $5094): the packet count is the first byte's low 3 bits, each 16-byte packet is sent through rP1 as a $00/$30 reset pulse, 128 bits (a 1 bit is written as $10, a 0 bit as $20, each followed by $30) and a stop bit
1F:5040.evidence: reading; Super Game Boy packet protocol (Pan Docs) for the bit pattern

00:05E2.name: DetectSGB
00:05E2.note: sends packet set $0B, reads rP1 with two different line selections and returns carry set when the joypad lines change as a Super Game Boy makes them; sends packet set $0A afterwards in both outcomes
00:05E2.evidence: reading; Super Game Boy packet protocol (Pan Docs) for the bit pattern

00:0692.name: DelayBCWhenSGB
00:0692.note: returns at once when wSGBActive is 0; otherwise busy-waits BC times about $06D6 loop passes

00:0796.name: TurnOffLCD
00:0796.note: if rLCDC bit 7 is set, waits for rLY = $91, then clears rLCDC bit 7 and bit 7 of wC5EC

00:06A8.name: SGBTransferCompressed
00:06A8.note: A = packet set index (stored in wSGBPacketIndex); returns at once when wSGBActive is 0; otherwise turns the LCD off, clears vTiles1, decompresses the stream at HL into vTiles1, fills the 20 x 13 corner of vBGMap0 with tiles $80, $81, ... in order, turns the LCD on, sends the packet set with SendSGBPacketSet and turns it off again; the tile data is thereby shown for the Super Game Boy to read
00:06A8.evidence: reading; Super Game Boy packet protocol (Pan Docs) for the bit pattern

00:0705.name: SGBTransferRaw
00:0705.note: A = packet set index; H = ROM bank, DE = source, BC = byte count: the same as SGBTransferCompressed, but copies the bytes to vTiles1 instead of decompressing
00:0705.evidence: reading; Super Game Boy packet protocol (Pan Docs) for the bit pattern

00:0829.name: UploadBGPalettes
00:0829.note: when bit 7 of wC526 is set, writes 8 bytes (one palette) from a buffer address derived by Func_000_0897 to rBGPD starting at index wC526; otherwise writes all 64 bytes from wC49F to rBGPD from index 0; each byte is written after waiting for VRAM access

00:3290.name: InitSoundHardware
00:3290.note: rNR52 = $80, rNR51 = 0, rNR50 = $77; sets the first two bytes of each of the 6 channel slots at wSoundChannelSlots to $FF; clears the 72 bytes at wSoundLabelSlots, wDD15 and wDD19; calls Func_000_32DB with BC = 0

00:0040.name: VBlankVector
00:0040.note: di; jp VBlankHandler (the interrupt vector at $0040)

00:03A4.name: VBlankHandler
00:03A4.note: runs once per frame: saves registers and the VRAM and WRAM banks; skips everything but the sound tick when wC5ED bit 0 shows it was entered again; otherwise runs the OAM DMA routine at $FF80, uploads queued palettes on CGB, flushes the queued BG map write, restores the DMG palettes, scroll and LCDC, applies the screen shake, polls the joypad, runs SoundTick, advances the random seed, processes the sound queue, runs GameFrameUpdate, steps the string display when wC52B is set, steps the fade, and increments the 16-bit frame counter wC5F0/wC5F1; resets the game when all four buttons are held

00:33E8.name: SoundTick
00:33E8.note: for each of the 6 channel slots at wSoundChannelSlots: copies the slot into HRAM $FFD8-$FFF7, reads events from the track in bank hSoundBank and writes the channel's sound registers (the per-frame sound engine; called from VBlankHandler)

00:131A.name: ProcessSoundQueue
00:131A.note: starts the music requested in wMusicRequest and the effect requested in wSoundEffectRequest (StartMusic / StartSoundEffect), then sets each request to $FF

00:1231.name: StartMusic
00:1231.note: A = sound id (0 = none): stores it in wC608, calls InitSoundHardware (silencing every channel), stores A in wSoundId and starts the track with Func_000_334E unless the id is one of a list that is handled separately

00:127C.name: StartSoundEffect
00:127C.note: A = sound id: stores it in wSoundId and starts the effect (ids in a fixed list take a separate path)

00:0474.name: GameFrameUpdate
00:0474.note: hOamNextEntry = 0, ComputeSpriteScrollOffsets, RunGameModeUpdate, and ClearUnusedOAMEntries unless a fade is running

00:048A.name: RunGameModeUpdate
00:048A.note: unless wC5DF is non-zero or a fade is running: jumps through a 9-entry table indexed by wGameMode to the mode's per-frame routine (modes 0-8 in banks $01, $02, $03, none, $31, $07, $24, $A0, $F2)

00:0355.name: RunGameModeInit
00:0355.note: jumps through a 9-entry table indexed by wGameMode to the mode's start-up routine (banks $01, $02, $03, none, $31, $07, $24, $A0, $F2); called from the main loop each time the mode changes

00:0BB4.name: ClearUnusedOAMEntries
00:0BB4.note: zeroes the first byte (Y) of every OAM shadow entry from hOamNextEntry up to 40

00:252D.name: ComputeSpriteScrollOffsets
00:252D.note: hFFD2/hFFD3 = -(hScrollX - 9) - 1 and hFFD4/hFFD5 = -(hScrollY - $11) - 1 as 16-bit values; returns early in game mode 1 when wC5DC & $0F = 6

00:0BCC.name: FlushQueuedBGMapWrite
00:0BCC.note: if wC0C0/wC0C1 (a VRAM address) is non-zero, writes wC0C3 bytes from wC0C4 there: along the row when wC0C2 is 0, down the column otherwise

00:04ED.name: ApplyScreenShake
00:04ED.note: while wC604 or wC605 is non-zero, counts it down and adds an oscillating offset (from the counter's low bits) to rSCY or rSCX

00:07FD.name: CopyDMGPalettesToHardware
00:07FD.note: rBGP, rOBP0, rOBP1 = wC5E9, wC5EA, wC5EB

00:07F1.name: WriteLCDCShadow
00:07F1.note: waits until rSTAT mode bits are 0, then rLCDC = wC5EC

00:0F4E.name: StepFade
00:0F4E.note: does nothing when wFadeState is 0; otherwise advances the palette fade by one step per call (CGB, SGB and DMG paths)

00:0A61.name: ReadJoypadDirect
00:0A61.note: B = the buttons: upper nibble D-pad (bit 7 down, 6 up, 5 left, 4 right), lower nibble A, B, Select, Start (bits 0-3), 1 = pressed; reads rP1 with each line group selected

00:0A17.name: PollJoypad
00:0A17.note: shifts wJoypadHeld to wJoypadHeldPrev and reads the new state into wJoypadHeld (directly, or through the SGB path when wSGBActive)

00:0A8D.name: UpdateJoypadPresses
00:0A8D.note: wJoypadPressed = buttons newly held since the last poll; wJoypadPressedRepeat = the same, plus an auto-repeat that fires after $14 frames and then every 6 (timer in wJoypadRepeatTimer)

02:541B.name: UpdatePlayerMovement
02:541B.note: does nothing during a fade or while the map is loading; reads the D-pad (wJoypadHeld, wJoypadPressed), sets the facing hPlayerFacing and the move timer hFF9A, and starts or continues a step when the tile ahead is free (checks through Func_002_59CD, Func_002_5A51 and Func_002_5AB6)

02:4FE8.name: CheckInteractionInFront
02:4FE8.note: when A is newly pressed and no fade, load or move is in progress: finds the position one step ahead of the player (hPlayerX or hPlayerY +/- 16 chosen by hPlayerFacing), looks it up with Func_002_59CD, and compares the result with the four ids at wC910 to pick an interaction

12:6EC6.note: unless the map is loading or wCBCF bit 7 is clear: reads the sprite entries starting at wCBCF (tile offset, set index with bit 7 selecting a sub index, attribute, position bytes), sets the hSprite inputs and 16-bit positions from them plus the scroll, and draws each with DrawMetaSprite

7F:700A.name: DrawMetaSprite
7F:700A.note: DE = Data_07F_7011 (the table of meta-sprite sets), then DrawMetaSpriteAt

7F:7065.name: DrawMetaSpriteAt
7F:7065.note: DE = table of set pointers: returns at once when hOamNextEntry is $27 or more; otherwise converts the 16-bit position (hSpriteOriginX with hFFAA, hSpriteOriginY with hFFAC) to screen coordinates by adding the scroll-offset words hSpriteScrollXLo/Hi and hSpriteScrollYLo/Hi, and writes OAM entries for the sprite chosen by hSpriteSetIndex and hSpriteSubIndex (tile += hSpriteTileOffset, attribute ^= hSpriteAttrXor)

02:59CD.name: TileBlockedAtPixel
02:59CD.note: B = X, C = Y in pixels: copies the four tile ids of the 2 x 2 block at tile (X / 8, Y / 8) of wScreenTileBuffer (rows of 20) to wC910-wC913; returns A = 1 when any of them is at most wC192, else A = 0 (a different pair of comparisons with wC196 runs when hFF8C bit 3 is set)

02:5A51.name: FindSpriteSlotAtTile
02:5A51.note: B = X, C = Y in pixels: returns A = the 1-based number of the first slot of wSpriteSlots (from wCB8A, count wSpriteSlotCount) whose X and Y bytes, or those plus 15, lie in the same 16-pixel cell as (B, C); A = 0 when none does

00:2391.name: PersonalityIndexOfRecord

The status screen passes this to the string database as a personality-name index (category 7, 27 names), so it is the monster's personality index (E-0031)

1A:4001.name: LoadSkillRecord
1A:4001.note: wCFEC/wCFED (the first word of the record buffer) = skill number: copies the 17-byte record at SkillTable + 17 * number (bank $1A, $40D4) to wCFEE

1A:4022.name: LoadSkillRecordPart

34:4001.name: LoadMonsterRecord
34:4001.note: wCFE6/wCFE7 = monster id: copies its 26-byte MonsterTable record to wCFEC (ids at or above $250 come from bank $A2 through Func_0A2_402D)

34:4040.name: LoadMonsterRecordTo
34:4040.note: DE = destination: like LoadMonsterRecord but copies the 26-byte record to [DE]

34:406E.name: CopyBytesDEFromHL
34:406E.note: B bytes from [HL] to [DE]; HL and DE advance

00:19A9.note: loads the screen at (hMapScreenX, hMapScreenY) of map hMapId: finds the map record (MapRecordPointer), picks one of its variants by the highest set bit of the flag byte whose RAM address is stored in the record, decompresses that variant's tile-map stream (an array of far pointers, indexed by row * width + column) into wScreenTileBuffer and, on CGB, the attribute stream into wD000 (WRAM bank 2); then runs the map's tile-replacement table (Func_084_43B8) and two map-specific fix-ups (Func_000_1B6F, Func_000_1A73); hands over to Func_061_4472 when wCC44 bit 7 is set

00:1D7F.name: MapRecordPointer

10:4001.note: one frame of the event-script engine: FetchScriptCommand, then ExecuteScriptCommand

10:4008.name: FetchScriptCommand
